title.value: Label fusion and training methods for reliable representation of inter-rater uncertainty
title.justification: The title is directly extracted from the provided paper metadata, outlining the focus on label fusion and training methods to handle inter-rater uncertainty, specifically in the context of medical imaging segmentation.
title.quote: Label fusion and training methods for reliable representation of inter-rater uncertainty

extractions.description: This paper explores different methods for fusing labels from multiple raters in medical imaging to address inter-rater variability and improve deep learning model reliability. It evaluates three label fusion approaches (STAPLE, averaging, random sampling) and compares them with traditional and SoftSeg training frameworks, across two medical imaging datasets, assessing calibration, uncertainty estimation, and segmentation performance.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on optimizing label fusion methods and training frameworks to improve the reliability of medical image segmentation, which is technological advancement in the medical field and not directly related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Reliable models generating calibrated outputs and reflecting the inter-rater disagreement are key to the integration of artificial intelligence in clinical practice.

primary_category.justification: The paper discusses medical image segmentation techniques and evaluation methods, which are outside the scope of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development categories.
primary_category.quote: Medical tasks are prone to inter-rater variability due to multiple factors such as image quality, professional experience and training, or guideline clarity.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no elements in the paper that address secondary Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes as it is entirely focused on medical imaging and deep learning techniques.
secondary_categories.quote: Training deep learning networks with annotations from multiple raters is a common practice that mitigates the model’s bias towards a single expert.
